Subject: Quick question on short pilot wrap & conversion options

Marcus — thanks again for the demo and the warm intro to token-level invoicing. We're at the end of week three of the 30-day pilot and our engineering team is hitting a limit on concurrent inference while the clinical UAT completes. Two asks: 1) if we need another week, what does that cost look like (days vs. credits)? and 2) if we convert to a committed package, what discount can apply retroactively to pilot consumption?

Samantha and I sketched two internal options: a straight 7-day extension billed pro-rata, or an incremental credit top-up (we call it a "burst bucket") that buys 48 hours of peak throughput. Which approach do you recommend to minimize friction with procurement?

—Alex
Product Lead, QuantaHealth
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick question on short pilot wrap & conversion options

Alex — great to hear the UAT is progressing. Short answer: we can do both, but they have different signals for procurement and sales.

High-level: a pro-rata 7-day extension is the fastest operationally (we simply extend the timebox and invoice for the additional days at the pilot rate). The burst-bucket (48h of peak throughput) gives you capacity without changing the end date, and maps cleanly to your engineers' need for concurrent headroom.

A third path we've been piloting with similar customers is a Runway Bridge Token (RBT): a small, non-refundable credit purchase that can convert into a one-time offset if you sign a conversion commitment within 30 days. For example: buy a $4k RBT now; if you sign a 12-month committed package within 30 days, we apply $3k of that as a conversion credit (10% conversion bonus). That gives QuantaHealth immediate runway and a tangible incentive to convert.

I'll assemble numbers for the two explicit options and the RBT model — copying Priya (covering commercial) and Karthik (ops/limits).

—Marcus
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Alex — attaching a usage snapshot from yesterday to help size the burst. Two concrete proposals below (numbers illustrative; final figures depend on the usage spike you attach):

Option A — 7-day pro-rata extension:
- Extends pilot to 2026-07-30 (adds 7 calendar days)
- Billed at pilot daily rate: $1,500/day -> $10,500 total
- No change to conversion incentives

Option B — Burst bucket (48h peak throughput):
- 48 hours of pre-provisioned peak capacity, consumable through pilot end
- One-time fee: $6,500 (covers expected peak tokens and concurrency)
- If converted within 30 days, we reduce first-month invoice by $4,000

Option C — RBT (Runway Bridge Token):
- Immediate purchase: $4,000 non-refundable RBT
- If QuantaHealth signs a 12-month committed package within 30 days, $3,000 of RBT applied against first invoice + 10% additional conversion credit applied in month 1
- Benefits: fastest procurement (PO for credits), minimal contract amendment

Operational notes: we can provision a burst within 2–4 hours after payment. Pro-rata extension requires a short addendum to the pilot, legal sign-off (1–2 business days), and will preserve current per-token rates.

Attachments: QuantaHealth_usage_snapshot_July15.csv

If you prefer, Marcus can route Option B or C through our procurement playbook to expedite PO language.

—Priya

Alex — quick operational clarifications on what we can toggle without legal:
- Burst bucket (Option B): yes, we can allow a 5-business-day liquidation window post-pilot to convert unused burst hours to invoice credit, provided the conversion is to a minimum commit (e.g., $60k ARR equivalent). We'll record that as a commercial note; legal doesn't need an addendum for that if you accept the T&Cs in the PO.
- RBT (Option C): conversion credit split across two invoices is ok — we'll mark the credit ledger as two applied credits (month 1 and month 2). The RBT itself is non-refundable unless conversion happens; when conversion happens we apply the agreed split.
- Pro-rata 7-day extension (Option A): requires a one-line addendum to the pilot SOW; legal turnaround ~24–48 hours.

I'll prepare a short PDF offer showing the three paths with exact dollar figures based on the attached usage. Naomi — can you confirm the templated PO language for an RBT purchase so Alex's procurement team can see exact line items?
